component.name: Archtoys
component.summary: PowerToys-style tools for Linux: pick colors, copy text, measure the screen

description.p: Archtoys is a growing set of small tools for Linux in one native app, inspired by Microsoft PowerToys. It works on Wayland and X11 and is at home on KDE Plasma.

ul.li: Pick any pixel on any monitor, with a magnifier and arrow keys for precision
See the color's name among about 32,000, and find colors by name
Copy it as HEX, RGB, HSL, HSV, OKLCH and more, edit and compare colors
Drag over any part of the screen and copy the text in it, even from images and videos
Languages are detected by themselves
Measure a box, the space around a point, a width or a height, in px, cm or inches
Keep up to three boxes on the screen and copy their sizes at once
Keep the computer from sleeping for a set time, until a time of day, or until you turn it off
Keep the screen on too, or only the computer, from its page or the tray
Screenshot to clipboard: drag over an area and it is copied as a picture
Image Resizer: resize and convert pictures from the file manager's right-click menu

description.p: Archtoys works offline. Text Extractor uses Tesseract and Image Resizer uses ImageMagick, installed when you turn them on, and Text Extractor downloads a language's data the first time it is needed.

screenshot.caption: Picking a color, with the magnifier next to the cursor

ul.li: CI: the package checks no longer fail at random when apt, dnf or pacman lists several versions
Archtoys starts fast again: the window shows about 5 times sooner than in v0.9.1 and v0.9.2
Image Resizer: a notification when it's done instead of a window (Settings, Micro-toys turns it off)
CI: the benchmark measures more times, for steadier numbers
Release: each new version is sent to Flathub as a pull request
Software centers and Flathub: the app's description lists each release and its changes
APT repository: its index no longer lists its own previous copy
CI: the APT package check shows apt's warnings when a version doesn't show up
Flatpak: built on the newer 26.08 runtime
Archtoys runs as a Flatpak, with every toy working, and updates from Flathub
The AppImage carries the app's description
Awake: keep the computer awake for as long as you choose
Image Resizer: resize and convert pictures from the file manager's right-click menu
An APT repository for Debian and Ubuntu
